literal: Piling up even if (they) come, despair he-who-has-not experienced trouble, trouble will suffer.
translation: The trouble experienced by a man who does not despair even when hardships come piling up, will itself suffer trouble.
modern: துன்பங்கள் ஒன்றன்பின் ஒன்றாக அடுக்கிக்கொண்டு வந்தாலும் மனம் தளராதவன் அடைந்த துன்பமே, அவனிடம் தோற்றுத் துன்பப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet personifies trouble to illustrate the power of a resilient mind. It states that if a person refuses to despair even when hardships come one after another, the hardship itself will suffer. The word 'அழிவு' (destruction) here refers to the breaking down or despair of the mind. By standing firm, the resilient person turns the tables, making 'இடுக்கண்' (trouble) experience 'இடுக்கண்' (trouble) and ultimately defeating it.
